newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch software firm ICT mulls Amsterdam listing.
newsitem.headline: Dutch software firm ICT mulls Amsterdam listing.

text.p: ICT Automatisering, a Dutch provider of software and software related services in high technology and industrial automation, hopes to apply for a listing on the Amsterdam stock exchange some time this year, the company said on Monday.

"Listing will give ICT access to the capital market, enabling the financing of future acquisitions. ICT also considers listing important to make its name more widely known," the company said in a statement.
ICT had turnover of 70 million guilders in 1996, a 12.6 percent increase on the previous year.
Net profit rose 11.5 percent to 7.2 million guilders. Net profit per share was 4.34 guilders per share, up from 4.28 in 1995. At the end of 1996, ICT had 1,650,000 shares outstanding.
Net margin was 10.2 percent, down from 1995's 10.3 percent.
MeesPierson will be lead manager and bookrunner of the listing.
ICT was founded in 1978, and operates from three sites in the Netherlands.
ICT's main activities include embedded software and production automation. The company employs 470 people.
A share option-programme for the employees will be introduced to enhance motivation, while the listing also gives current shareholders a way out, the company said.
